### Complete the potential-outcomes table

A city randomly assigns people seeking employment to one of two programs. Let $A=1$ denote assignment to an intensive job-training program and $A=0$ denote assignment to standard job-search materials. Let $Y=1$ if the person is employed six months later and $Y=0$ otherwise.

For each person, $Y(1)$ is the employment outcome if assigned to job training, and $Y(0)$ is the employment outcome if assigned to the standard materials. Use consistency to complete as much of the table as possible. Enter a question mark for any potential outcome that cannot be determined from the observed data.

<table class="compact-data-table potential-outcomes-table">
<caption>Observed assignments and employment outcomes for five participants.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th scope="col">Person</th><th scope="col">$A$</th><th scope="col">$Y$</th><th scope="col">$Y(0)$</th><th scope="col">$Y(1)$</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td></tr>
<tr><td>3</td><td>1</td><td>0</td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td></tr>
<tr><td>4</td><td>0</td><td>1</td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td></tr>
<tr><td>5</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td><td><span aria-label="blank to be completed">_____</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

::: {.answer-block}
**Solution**

<table class="compact-data-table potential-outcomes-table">
<caption>Potential outcomes that can be determined from the observed data.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th scope="col">Person</th><th scope="col">$A$</th><th scope="col">$Y$</th><th scope="col">$Y(0)$</th><th scope="col">$Y(1)$</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>?</td><td>1</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>?</td></tr>
<tr><td>3</td><td>1</td><td>0</td><td>?</td><td>0</td></tr>
<tr><td>4</td><td>0</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>?</td></tr>
<tr><td>5</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>?</td><td>1</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

For a person assigned to job training ($A=1$), consistency tells us that $Y(1)=Y$. For a person assigned to the standard materials ($A=0$), consistency tells us that $Y(0)=Y$. The other potential outcome remains unknown for every person.
:::
